Stage Settings The ‘stage’ represents Clare’s cell in her monastery at San Damiano. It is split like a triangle into 3 sections around the font in the centre. For the sake of a unified language, let's call these the ‘three stations of her cell’. The first station ( facing the audience directly on all sides at the top of the font) is a small clothes rack and a simple chair. The second station ( down stage right) is a straw mat where she sleeps. The Third Station ( down stage left) is a little table with a chair) Clare plays and performs intermittently between the three stations. Francis, a primary character in the play, walks in between these stations as if a memory in her mind. He sits on the stage right of the sanctuary. But for the beginning of the show, father is seated in the pews. A two person choir sits stage left of the altar. Most of the action takes place below the sanctuary around the three stations of the cell.
Scene 1: Christ on the Cross

column2: CLARE: Blessed be the Lord Jesus Christ. Silence. You did not leave me. She smiles.
I heard them all. The singing. The prayers. All those solemnities... I was there.
She looks around her cell. And yet... I was here.
Beat. Thank you, Lord. She kneels in prayer.
SOUND: Then, slowly, everything fades except the sound of her breathing and her heart beat.
Hymn: Make me a channel of your peace replays and transitions into the next act.

Third Letter— PART TWO ACTION: Clare has reached the peak of her frailty. She is kneeling and recites the third letter. As if in prayer to Agnes. As if her thoughts could telepath and Agnes would receive her words.

column2: OLDER CLARE (letter three): My beloved Agnes, Hold fast to what you have begun. ( she coughs) Hold fast to Christ. (she stands up weakly)
Look upon Him. (she looks to Christ, back towards the audience) Consider Him. Contemplate Him.

He whom the heavens cannot contain has chosen to dwell within you (she turns to address the audience) So make room for Him. If you suffer with Him ( she almost falls over ) Oh my, God give me strength
If you suffer with him, you will share in His glory. Keep looking at Him. Keep walking.
Your sister, Clare.

column2: CLARE: We are coming close to the ending of my story. (She sits on her stool.)

You might wonder, ‘But why Clare? Must we live to suffer?’ I invite you to imagine now. Imagine giving up everything- having nothing to your name. No wealth, no property, no shoes on your feet even- nothing. Nothing belongs to you on this Earth.
What is left in that nothingness? Ah now I see, you see.
In that nothingness, there is still Christ. This is what it is to suffer. This is the privilege of poverty.
(she looks up at Christ)
Remember how I said, I was born into a life written for me? In this same way, even in the church of my time, as a woman, life was already written for us.

I wanted so much to live in the privilege of poverty (Privilegium Paupertatis), and The sisters and I desperately wanted to be given the right to live with no possession of anything material- property, land- absolutely nothing.

To live simply by the goodwill of the donation of alms. But at the time, The Pope, even though fond of me, as I was of him, was worried that as women, we would not be able to manage this extreme poverty. That as women, we needed to have corporate ownership, land for farming at least in order to sustain ourselves.
I had to unwrite the life written for women in monastic living and write a new rule. I demanded the right to live in the privilege of poverty.

CLARE ( FOURTH LETTER) : Clare writes and her words are shown on the screen as if it were a touch phone screen. She types only the first few sentences.
Media & said by Clare: My beloved sister Agnes of Prague,

When the world becomes noisy or confusing, remember where your heart belongs. Place your mind in the mirror of eternity. Place your soul in the splendour of heaven. Place your heart in Christ. Look at Him until you become like Him. He gave Himself completely for you. So give yourself completely to Him.

column2: ( She walks to the font and gazes into it as a mirror) ( The media stops displaying the text)
And remember Mary, who carried Christ within her. You too can carry Him within your heart.

Our blessed Father Francis taught us to fast, but remember, each of you, that our flesh is not made of bronze, nor our strength of stone. I know how severely some of you fast, in your own ways. Do not be so hard on yourselves. We must care for the body so that we may continue to praise the Lord.
Our poverty is not punishment. Your poverty is not punishment. It is your gift. It is love.
Rejoice, each and all of you. Remember to carry Christ within you. And remember me, remember me and my sisters in your prayers. Always, Your sister in Christ, Clare.

CLARE: I have spent my life learning to gaze. Not to possess. Not to hold, not even to be held… Only to remain. To look upon him, until I became, little by little, what I was looking at.
